captions.text: The Book Which Tells the Truth, by Raël.
captions.speaker: AudioplayNarrator

captions.text: First published in French in 1974.
captions.speaker: AudioplayNarrator

captions.text: This is a Wheel of Heaven audio play.
captions.speaker: AudioplayNarrator

captions.text: In December 1973, the French journalist and racing driver Claude Vorilhon — Raël — reports a series of encounters with an extraterrestrial being named Yahweh, inside a volcanic crater in central France.
captions.speaker: AudioplayNarrator

captions.text: Over six mornings, Yahweh reads the Bible with him line by line, and teaches him that life on Earth was created in laboratories by a human civilization from another planet: the Elohim.
captions.speaker: AudioplayNarrator

captions.text: You will hear three voices.
captions.speaker: AudioplayNarrator

captions.text: Raël as the narrator, writing after the encounters ended, looking back.
captions.speaker: AudioplayNarrator

captions.text: Raël inside the encounters, asking his questions in real time.
captions.speaker: AudioplayNarrator

captions.text: And Yahweh, teaching — his voice carries a subtle hall reverb to mark his off-world origin.
captions.speaker: AudioplayNarrator

captions.text: The book begins now.
captions.speaker: AudioplayNarrator

captions.text: Since the age of nine, I have had only one passion: motor racing.
captions.speaker: Narrator

captions.text: If I created a magazine devoted to this field three years ago, it was so I could live in that thrilling milieu where a person seeks to surpass himself by surpassing others.
captions.speaker: Narrator

captions.text: From my earliest childhood I dreamed of being a racing driver one day, following in Fangio’s footsteps.
captions.speaker: Narrator

captions.text: Thanks to the contacts my magazine brought me, I was able to race myself—and generally with some success; a dozen trophies now adorn my apartment.
captions.speaker: Narrator

captions.text: On the morning of December 13, 1973, when I headed into the volcanoes overlooking Clermont-Ferrand, it was more to breathe some fresh air than to drive.
captions.speaker: Narrator

captions.text: And after a year spent following races, from circuit to circuit, living almost all the time on four wheels, my legs were itching.
captions.speaker: Narrator

captions.text: The air was crisp and the sky rather gray, with a base of mist.
captions.speaker: Narrator

captions.text: I walked and did a bit of jogging.
captions.speaker: Narrator

captions.text: I had left the path where I had parked my car and set myself the goal of reaching the center of the crater of the Puy de Lassolas, where I often went in summer to picnic with my family.
captions.speaker: Narrator

captions.text: What a magnificent and exhilarating place.
captions.speaker: Narrator

captions.text: To think that a few thousand years ago, right where my feet touched the ground, lava was gushing at incredibly high temperatures…
captions.speaker: Narrator

captions.text: Among the scoria you can still find very decorative volcanic bombs.
captions.speaker: Narrator

captions.text: The stunted vegetation is a little reminiscent of Provence—minus the sun…
captions.speaker: Narrator

captions.text: I was about to leave and took one last look at the summit of the circular mountain made by heaps of scoria.
captions.speaker: Narrator

captions.text: How many times I had amused myself by sliding, as if on skis, down those steep slopes.
captions.speaker: Narrator

captions.text: Suddenly, through the mist, I noticed a flashing red light, then a sort of helicopter descending toward me.
captions.speaker: Narrator

captions.text: But a helicopter makes noise—and here I could hear absolutely nothing, not even the faintest whistle.
captions.speaker: Narrator

captions.text: A balloon?
captions.speaker: Narrator

captions.text: The craft was now about twenty meters up, and I realized it was flattened in shape.
captions.speaker: Narrator

captions.text: A flying saucer!
captions.speaker: Narrator

captions.text: I had believed in them firmly for a long time, but I had never hoped to see one myself.
captions.speaker: Narrator

captions.text: It was about seven meters in diameter, flat below and conical above, about two and a half meters high.
captions.speaker: Narrator

captions.text: At its base a violent red light flashed, and at its top an intermittent white light recalled a camera flash.
captions.speaker: Narrator

captions.text: That white light was so intense I couldn’t look at it without blinking.
captions.speaker: Narrator

captions.text: The craft continued to descend without a sound and came to a stop two meters above the ground.
captions.speaker: Narrator

captions.text: I was petrified and remained absolutely motionless.
captions.speaker: Narrator

captions.text: I wasn’t afraid, but filled with joy to be living such a moment.
captions.speaker: Narrator

captions.text: I bitterly regretted not having a camera.
captions.speaker: Narrator

captions.text: Then the incredible happened: a hatch opened beneath the craft and a kind of stairway unfolded to the ground.
captions.speaker: Narrator

captions.text: I understood that a being was about to emerge, and I wondered what it would look like.
captions.speaker: Narrator

captions.text: Two feet appeared, then two legs, which reassured me a little, for it seemed I was about to deal with a man.
captions.speaker: Narrator

captions.text: What I first took for a child finally appeared completely, came down the steps, and walked straight toward me.
captions.speaker: Narrator

captions.text: I then saw that it was not a child, despite a height of around one meter twenty.
captions.speaker: Narrator

captions.text: He had slightly slanted eyes, long black hair, and a small black beard.
captions.speaker: Narrator

captions.text: He stopped about ten meters from me.
captions.speaker: Narrator

captions.text: I still hadn’t moved.
captions.speaker: Narrator

captions.text: He wore a green one-piece suit covering his whole body, and though his head seemed bare, a strange halo surrounded it—not exactly a halo, more as if the air around his face shone faintly and vibrated.
captions.speaker: Narrator

captions.text: It was like an invisible diving helmet, a bubble so thin you could hardly see it.
captions.speaker: Narrator

captions.text: His skin was white with a slight greenish tinge, like a man with a bad liver.
captions.speaker: Narrator

captions.text: He smiled faintly at me.
captions.speaker: Narrator

captions.text: I thought the best thing was to answer his smile.
captions.speaker: Narrator

captions.text: I was not at ease.
captions.speaker: Narrator

captions.text: I smiled back and inclined my head slightly in greeting.
captions.speaker: Narrator

captions.text: He replied with the same gesture.
captions.speaker: Narrator

captions.text: Thinking I should see if he could hear me, I asked him:
captions.speaker: Narrator

captions.text: Where do you come from?
captions.speaker: Raël

captions.text: He answered in a powerful voice, very clearly articulated but slightly nasal:
captions.speaker: Narrator

captions.text: From very far away…
captions.speaker: Yahweh

captions.text: Do you speak French?
captions.speaker: Raël

captions.text: I speak all the languages of the world.
captions.speaker: Yahweh

captions.text: Do you come from another planet?
captions.speaker: Raël

captions.text: Yes.
captions.speaker: Yahweh

captions.text: As he spoke, he had moved to within about two meters of me.
captions.speaker: Narrator

captions.text: Is this the first time you have come to Earth?
captions.speaker: Raël

captions.text: Oh no!
captions.speaker: Yahweh

captions.text: Have you come here very often?
captions.speaker: Raël

captions.text: Very often… to say the least.
captions.speaker: Yahweh

captions.text: What do you come here to do?
captions.speaker: Raël

captions.text: Today, to speak to you.
captions.speaker: Yahweh

captions.text: To me?
captions.speaker: Raël

captions.text: Yes.
captions.speaker: Yahweh

captions.text: To you, Claude Vorilhon, editor of a small motor-sport magazine, married, father of two children.
captions.speaker: Yahweh

captions.text: How do you know all that?
captions.speaker: Raël

captions.text: We have been observing you for a long time.
captions.speaker: Yahweh

captions.text: Why me?
captions.speaker: Raël

captions.text: That is exactly what I want to tell you.
captions.speaker: Yahweh

captions.text: Why did you come here on this cold winter morning?
captions.speaker: Yahweh

captions.text: I don’t know…
captions.speaker: Narrator

captions.text: I felt like taking a little walk in the open air…
captions.speaker: Narrator

captions.text: Do you come here often?
captions.speaker: Yahweh

captions.text: In summer, yes, but at this time of year hardly ever.
captions.speaker: Raël

captions.text: Then why today?
captions.speaker: Yahweh

captions.text: Had you planned this walk long in advance?
captions.speaker: Yahweh

captions.text: No. I don’t know.
captions.speaker: Raël

captions.text: This morning when I woke up I suddenly felt like coming here.
captions.speaker: Raël

captions.text: You came because I wanted to see you.
captions.speaker: Yahweh

captions.text: Do you believe in telepathy?
captions.speaker: Yahweh

captions.text: Yes, of course.
captions.speaker: Raël

captions.text: It has always interested me, as has everything connected with what men call ‘flying saucers’.
captions.speaker: Raël

captions.text: I never thought I would see one myself.
captions.speaker: Raël

captions.text: Well then, I used telepathy to make you come here.
captions.speaker: Yahweh

captions.text: I have many things to tell you.
captions.speaker: Yahweh

captions.text: Have you read the Bible?
captions.speaker: Yahweh

captions.text: Yes.
captions.speaker: Raël

captions.text: Why do you ask me that?
captions.speaker: Raël

captions.text: Did you read it a long time ago?
captions.speaker: Yahweh

captions.text: No, I bought it only a few days ago.
captions.speaker: Raël

captions.text: Why?
captions.speaker: Yahweh

captions.text: I don’t know—suddenly I felt like reading it…
captions.speaker: Raël

captions.text: Again by telepathy I made you buy it.
captions.speaker: Yahweh

captions.text: I have many things to tell you, and I have chosen you for a difficult mission.
captions.speaker: Yahweh

captions.text: Come into my craft; we will be more comfortable there for a little chat.
captions.speaker: Yahweh

captions.text: I followed him and climbed the small staircase underneath the craft.
captions.speaker: Narrator

captions.text: Seen closer, it looked somewhat like a flattened bell with a solid, domed underside.
captions.speaker: Narrator

captions.text: Inside there were two armchairs facing each other, and the temperature was mild even though the door was open.
captions.speaker: Narrator

captions.text: There was no lamp, but a natural light that seemed to come from everywhere.
captions.speaker: Narrator

captions.text: There were no instruments suggesting a cockpit.
captions.speaker: Narrator

captions.text: The floor was made of a sparkling, slightly bluish alloy.
captions.speaker: Narrator

captions.text: Once I had sat down in the larger but lower armchair, made of a single slightly transparent, colorless, and very comfortable material, the little man sat facing me in a similar seat, smaller but higher so that his face was level with mine.
captions.speaker: Narrator

captions.text: He then touched part of the wall, and the whole craft became transparent, except for its base and its top.
captions.speaker: Narrator

captions.text: We were as if in the open air, but in a gentle warmth.
captions.speaker: Narrator

captions.text: He suggested I take off my coat, which I did, and he spoke.
captions.speaker: Narrator

captions.text: You very much regret not having a camera to tell all men about our meeting, with proof to back it up, don’t you?
captions.speaker: Yahweh

captions.text: Of course…
captions.speaker: Raël

captions.text: Listen to me.
captions.speaker: Yahweh

captions.text: You will tell them—but you will tell them the truth about what they are and what we are.
captions.speaker: Yahweh

captions.text: Depending on their reactions, we shall see whether we can show ourselves to them freely and officially.
captions.speaker: Yahweh

captions.text: Wait until you know everything before speaking to them, so that you can defend yourself properly against those who will not believe you, and so that you can bring them indisputable evidence.
captions.speaker: Yahweh

captions.text: You will write down everything I tell you and have the book containing these writings published.
captions.speaker: Yahweh

captions.text: Why did you choose me?
captions.speaker: Raël

captions.text: For many reasons.
captions.speaker: Yahweh

captions.text: First, we needed someone in a country where new ideas are well received and it is possible to express them.
captions.speaker: Yahweh

captions.text: France is the country where democracy was born, and its image throughout the world is that of the land of liberty.
captions.speaker: Yahweh

captions.text: Next, we needed someone intelligent and open to everything.
captions.speaker: Yahweh

captions.text: Finally—and above all—we needed someone who is a free-thinker without being anti-religious.
captions.speaker: Yahweh

captions.text: With a Jewish father and a Catholic mother, you happen to be the ideal link between two peoples very important in the history of the world.
captions.speaker: Yahweh

captions.text: Moreover, your occupation does not predispose you in any way to revelations that most would find unbelievable, which will make your words more credible.
captions.speaker: Yahweh

captions.text: Not being a scientist, you will not complicate matters and will explain them simply.
captions.speaker: Yahweh

captions.text: Not being a literary man, you will not write convoluted sentences that are hard for most people to read.
captions.speaker: Yahweh

captions.text: Lastly, we decided to choose someone after the first atomic explosion, which took place in 1945, and you were born in 1946.
captions.speaker: Yahweh

captions.text: We have been watching you since your birth—and even before.
captions.speaker: Yahweh

captions.text: That is why we have chosen you.
captions.speaker: Yahweh

captions.text: Do you have any other questions to ask me?
captions.speaker: Yahweh

captions.text: Where do you come from?
captions.speaker: Raël

captions.text: From a distant planet about which I will tell you nothing, for fear that, if the people of Earth were not wise, they might disturb our tranquility.
captions.speaker: Yahweh

captions.text: Is it very far away?
captions.speaker: Raël

captions.text: Very far; when I tell you the distance, you will understand that you cannot go there with your current technical and scientific knowledge.
captions.speaker: Yahweh

captions.text: What is your name?
captions.speaker: Raël

captions.text: We are men like you, and we live on a planet quite similar to Earth.
captions.speaker: Yahweh

captions.text: How long does it take you to come to Earth?
captions.speaker: Raël

captions.text: As long as it takes to think of it.
captions.speaker: Yahweh

captions.text: Why do you come to Earth?
captions.speaker: Raël

captions.text: To see how men are getting on and to watch over them.
captions.speaker: Yahweh

captions.text: They are the future; we are the past.
captions.speaker: Yahweh

captions.text: Are there many of you?
captions.speaker: Raël

captions.text: More than you.
captions.speaker: Yahweh

captions.text: I would like to go to your planet—could I?
captions.speaker: Raël

captions.text: No. First, you could not live there.
captions.speaker: Yahweh

captions.text: The atmosphere is very different from yours, and you are not sufficiently trained to withstand the journey.
captions.speaker: Yahweh

captions.text: Why meet here?
captions.speaker: Raël

captions.text: Because a volcano’s crater is an ideal place to be safe from prying eyes.
captions.speaker: Yahweh

captions.text: Now I am going to leave.
captions.speaker: Yahweh

captions.text: Come back tomorrow with the Bible, at the same time, and bring something to take notes with.
captions.speaker: Yahweh

captions.text: Bring nothing metallic with you, and speak to no one about our meetings, otherwise we shall not see each other again.
captions.speaker: Yahweh

captions.text: He let me go back down the little stairway, handed me my coat, and waved goodbye.
captions.speaker: Narrator

captions.text: The stairway folded up, the hatch closed without the slightest sound, and, still without a murmur or even the faintest whistle, the craft rose gently to about four hundred meters, then disappeared into the mist.
captions.speaker: Narrator
